name: Far right
summary: Comparative scholarship defines the far right by nativism (a state for natives, hostility to non-natives), authoritarianism (law and order, traditional values, strong leaders) and, for the populist radical right, anti-establishment populism. Scholars divide the family on democracy: the radical right accepts democratic procedure but strains liberal democracy, the extreme right rejects it. Bobbio places the extreme right as anti-liberal and anti-egalitarian. Economics is not part of the definition.
scope: A family, answered only from defining scholarship (Mudde on nativism, authoritarianism, populism; Bobbio on left and right; Arzheimer's presentation of Mudde's extreme/radical right terms; ECPS vocabulary entry summarising the literature). No member party programme or thinker is used. Fascism, neo-Nazism and the alt-right have their own entries.
